findings.detail: The changelog (lines 3-11) and hardware-support.md (head 332-337) add `PromptPieceTokenStore`, which keeps token IDs for chat-template pieces between requests. It is keyed by prefix-cache scope and holds up to 32 MiB per loaded tokenizer. This retains A-001-derived plaintext in process heap after a request finishes. T-028 covers residual GPU/KV memory and T-041 covers the SSD prefix tier, but neither covers this store. It also adds a second hit/miss timing signal: changelog line 9 cites 5-8 ms versus 102-264 ms preparation. If the scope key is the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, this stays inside the same-account exposure SEC-035 already accepts. If it uses a weaker key, such as model only or a caller-supplied field, it becomes a cross-tenant prefix-confirmation oracle. Trigger: a consumer replays a guessed conversation prefix and measures TTFT. Impact: confirms another tenant's prompt content. Fix: key the store strictly on the authenticated cacheSalt/scope, never caller fields. Clear it on model unload and KEK/cache wipe. Record it under T-041/T-028 with its lifetime, its bound and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 kill switch.
findings.title: New cross-request in-memory store of prompt-derived token pieces is not in the threat model

findings.detail: Head lines 1030-1046 document a new `PromptTokenCache` that keeps token IDs of rendered prompt pieces and reuses them for later requests in the same prefix-cache scope. Those cached pieces are derived from consumer prompts (A-001). T-041 covers only the encrypted SSD KV tier and its TTL, disk budget and KEK purge. T-028 covers residual GPU/KV memory. Neither covers this host-RAM cache. The doc gives no retention bound (TTL, size or eviction) and no purge on unload or logout. Reuse also shortens tokenization time for a repeated piece, which adds a second hit/miss latency signal. That signal would fall within the SEC-035 same-scope oracle only if scoping really uses the coordinator-authored cacheSalt rather than a caller field. Trigger: a same-scope co-tenant probes guessed history pieces, or an operator inspects process memory (ADV-001, T-014). Fix: record this cache in T-041/T-028 with its scope source, size/TTL bounds and purge points. Confirm the scope key comes from the coordinator and that `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0` disables it.
findings.title: New in-memory PromptTokenCache retains prompt-derived token IDs without threat-model coverage
